The most common reason is that the *parent* re-renders, which by default makes React re-render all its children, even if their props didn't actually change.

Check whether the parent is creating new objects or functions on every render — like inline event handlers, array literals, or object props. React treats these as "new" props each time, even if the values are identical. If the parent is passing `{ id: 5 }` as a prop instead of storing it, that object is recreated on every render.

To check if props are actually changing, wrap your child in `React.memo` and add a simple console log — if the props object reference stays the same (same identity in memory), then memoization will skip the re-render. If it changes, you've found where the new object is coming from. Move object and function creation outside the component, or use `useCallback` and `useMemo` in the parent to keep them stable.
